purpose: V3.5.1 (level 1) is FAIL. apps/web/app/api/platform-v7/cabinet-session/route.ts is the last route acting on an ambient cookie credential that is reachable by this programme: it reads pc_access_token through cookies(), verifies the role from it, and ISSUES an 8-hour pc_v7_cabinet session cookie. A cross-site page could make a signed-in visitor's browser mint itself a cabinet session - a state change, not a read. This closes that route on both sides and brings the route census in the V3.5.1 record up to what the tree actually contains.
requiredInvariants: V3.5.1 is NOT claimed and stays FAIL. One route of the fifteen is closed. The accounting proxy and the two settlement money proxies remain, and the named counterexample in the decision is unchanged.

No path owned by any active project lock is touched. Verified by running scripts/verify-pc-crop-project-lock.mjs on this branch: exit 0, failures empty. PC-CROP-FEDERAL-ACCOUNTING owns apps/web/app/platform-v7/accounting/ and apps/web/app/api/platform-v7/accounting/; this pass touches neither.

The V3.5.1 decision's condition is deliberately left pointing at the accounting route, which is still genuinely unguarded on main. Re-pointing it here would have been unnecessary and would have collided with the blocked pass that also edits this decision.
The existing double-submit mechanism is reused as-is: assertCsrf from server-request-security on the server, applyCsrfHeader from lib/csrf on the client. No new anti-forgery scheme is invented.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No schema change, no migration, no dependency, no lockfile change. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: The route was confirmed live and state-changing before being touched, not assumed from its name: it reads ACCESS_TOKEN_COOKIE through cookies(), resolves a verified role, signs a cabinet session and sets pc_v7_cabinet with an 8-hour maxAge.

The change cannot break a call that currently succeeds, and this was established by reading rather than asserted: apps/web/lib/server/auth-session-response.ts sets CSRF_COOKIE in the same response as ACCESS_COOKIE, so any session capable of passing the route's verified-role check already carries the token cookie.

The gate is placed before request.json() and before the credential is read, and a test asserts that ordering by index rather than trusting it - a check after the credential read would mean the request had already been parsed and the visitor's credential already consumed.
The single frontend caller was found by search and taught to send the token: components/platform-v7/LoginLegacyOverlay.tsx, using the same applyCsrfHeader helper the other guarded callers use.

Six cases: no header at all; cookie without header; header not matching the cookie (asserting reason csrf_mismatch, so absence and mismatch stay distinguishable); a matching pair passing the gate and failing later for a DIFFERENT reason, so 'refuse everything' cannot pass as success; the ordering assertion; and the caller actually sending the token.

Three mutations, each caught by exactly the intended case: removing the server gate fails 4 of 6; moving the gate after the credential read fails the ordering case; removing the header from the client fails the caller case.

The route census in the V3.5.1 record is brought up to the tree and the two earlier undercounts are recorded rather than quietly replaced: 23 (assertCsrf only), then 16 (per-file grep missing a defence that lives in an imported helper), now 14 with imports followed one level - 59 mutating routes, 38 direct, 2 via the staff command proxy, 5 Fetch Metadata, 14 neither. Every one of the 14 was read, and the record now says why most of them should NOT get a token: three unconditional stubs, two disabled in production before reaching a cookie, one no-op acknowledgement, three public intake forms, two server-to-server callbacks.

web tsc --noEmit exit 0. verify-decision-evidence 0. verify-web-unit-coverage 0 with the new spec in the executed list and the registry counts corrected to 20/914. Matrix unchanged at PASS 126 / FAIL 93 / NOT_APPLICABLE 88 / NOT_ASSESSED 38, and V3.5.1 still reads FAIL.
